discovery: Discovery of the third neutrino mixing angle (theta13) through electron-neutrino appearance and reactor antineutrino disappearance

nominees.name: Yifang Wang

motivation: After atmospheric and solar oscillations were established, the last unknown mixing angle, theta13, decided whether leptonic CP violation could ever be measured. In 2011 the T2K experiment, conceived and led by Koichiro Nishikawa, sent a muon-neutrino beam from J-PARC to Super-Kamiokande and saw the first indication of electron-neutrino appearance. In 2012 the Daya Bay experiment, led by Yifang Wang and Kam-Biu Luk, used carefully designed identical near and far detectors to observe reactor antineutrino disappearance at more than five sigma, measuring a surprisingly large theta13. Together these results completed the three-flavour mixing picture and opened the path to CP-violation searches at T2K, NOvA, Hyper-Kamiokande, DUNE and JUNO, a question that may explain the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the Universe. This work is a model of patient, precise experimental physics pointing beyond the Standard Model.
